decisions.question: Scope and manner of the general presentation
decisions.resolution: Keep dergestalt dass explicit, the attempted completeness in every assessment respect, American languages in general and differences among individual languages; no common-origin claim is added.

decisions.question: Principal inclusion, coordinated omissions and sound designation
decisions.resolution: Choose parts of the presentation provisionally, retaining the language-parts alternative. Preserve the two omitted categories and apposition; use specific designation by sounds while recording notation of sounds as an unresolved alternative.

decisions.question: Fragmented description and impossible complete overview
decisions.resolution: Retain the admitted cost to individual-language description and the claim that a complete structural overview becomes impossible under this procedure.

decisions.question: Comparative placement and appraisal of characteristics
decisions.resolution: Keep every characteristic of each individual language and comparison with the characteristics of the others; preserve appraised as valuative rather than merely descriptive.

decisions.question: Qualified high valuation of this advantage
decisions.resolution: Keep however internal, this very advantage emphatic, and scarcely able to rate too highly; do not reverse or turn the qualification into an absolute.

decisions.question: Effort, indecision and historical comparative valuation
decisions.resolution: Keep the language as bearer, effort and continued indecision, both connected questions, the study as a whole and the merits/shortcomings to be mutually weighed. Attribute the valuation to Humboldt without supplying a modern metric.

decisions.question: Partial recovery through a collating index
decisions.resolution: Keep nevertheless and to some extent, recovering the overview by an index that brings material together; do not invent its format or claim complete recovery.
